verses.english: Linked Discourses 22.87
9. Senior Mendicants
With Vakkali

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā vakkali kumbhakāranivesane viharati ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno.
verses.english: Now at that time Venerable Vakkali was staying in a potter’s shed, and he was sick, suffering, gravely ill.

verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā vakkali upaṭṭhāke āmantesi:
verses.english: Then he addressed his carers,

verses.pali: “etha tumhe, āvuso, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamatha; upasaṅkamitvā mama vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatha:
verses.english: “Please, reverends, go to the Buddha, and in my name bow with your head to his feet. Say to him:

verses.pali: ‘vakkali, bhante, bhikkhu ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno, so bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatī’ti.
verses.english: ‘Sir, the mendicant Vakkali is sick, suffering, and gravely ill. He bows with his head to your feet.’
And then say:

verses.pali: ‘sādhu kira, bhante, bhagavā yena vakkali bhikkhu tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṁ upādāyā’”ti.
verses.english: ‘Sir, please go to the mendicant Vakkali out of sympathy.’”

verses.pali: “Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato vakkalissa paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
verses.english: “Yes, reverend,” those monks replied. They did as he asked.

verses.pali: “vakkali, bhante, bhikkhu ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno, so bhagavato pāde sirasā vandati;
‘sādhu kira, bhante, bhagavā yena vakkali bhikkhu tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṁ upādāyā’”ti.

verses.english: The Buddha consented with silence.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yenāyasmā vakkali tenupasaṅkami.
verses.english: Then the Buddha robed up and, taking his bowl and robes, went to Venerable Vakkali.

verses.pali: Addasā kho āyasmā vakkali bhagavantaṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ. Disvāna mañcake samadhosi.
verses.english: Venerable Vakkali saw the Buddha coming off in the distance and stirred in his cot.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ vakkaliṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: But the Buddha said to him,
“It’s all right, Vakkali, don’t get up.
There are some seats spread out, I will sit there.”

verses.pali: Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane. Nisajja kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ vakkaliṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: He sat on the seat spread out and said to Vakkali,

verses.pali: “kacci te, vakkali, khamanīyaṁ, kacci yāpanīyaṁ, kacci dukkhā vedanā paṭikkamanti, no abhikkamanti; paṭikkamosānaṁ paññāyati, no abhikkamo”ti?
verses.english: “I hope you’re keeping well, Vakkali; I hope you’re all right. And I hope the pain is fading, not growing, that its fading is evident, not its growing.”

verses.pali: “Na me, bhante, khamanīyaṁ, na yāpanīyaṁ; bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṁ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo”ti.
verses.english: “Sir, I’m not all right, I’m not getting by. My pain is terrible and growing, not fading; its growing is apparent, not its fading.”

verses.pali: “Kacci te, vakkali, na kiñci kukkuccaṁ, na koci vippaṭisāro”ti?
verses.english: “I hope you don’t have any remorse or regret?”

verses.pali: “Taggha me, bhante, anappakaṁ kukkuccaṁ, anappako vippaṭisāro”ti.
verses.english: “Indeed, sir, I have no little remorse and regret.”

verses.pali: “Kacci pana taṁ, vakkali, attā sīlato na upavadatī”ti?
verses.english: “I hope you have no reason to blame yourself when it comes to ethical conduct?”

verses.pali: “Na kho maṁ, bhante, attā sīlato upavadatī”ti.
verses.english: “No sir, I have no reason to blame myself when it comes to ethical conduct.”

verses.pali: “No ce kira taṁ, vakkali, attā sīlato upavadati; atha kiñca te kukkuccaṁ ko ca vippaṭisāro”ti?
verses.english: “In that case, Vakkali, why do you have remorse and regret?”

verses.pali: “Cirapaṭikāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavantaṁ dassanāya upasaṅkamitukāmo, natthi ca me kāyasmiṁ tāvatikā balamattā, yāvatāhaṁ bhagavantaṁ dassanāya upasaṅkameyyan”ti.
verses.english: “For a long time I’ve wanted to go and see the Buddha, but I was physically too weak.”

verses.pali: “Alaṁ, vakkali, kiṁ te iminā pūtikāyena diṭṭhena?
verses.english: “Enough, Vakkali! Why would you want to see this rotting body?

verses.pali: Yo kho, vakkali, dhammaṁ passati so maṁ passati;
verses.english: One who sees the teaching sees me.

verses.pali: yo maṁ passati so dhammaṁ passati.
verses.english: One who sees me sees the teaching.
Seeing the teaching, you see me.
Seeing me, you see the teaching.
What do you think, Vakkali?
Is form permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

verses.pali: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
verses.english: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

verses.pali: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, kallaṁ nu taṁ samanupassituṁ:
verses.english: “But if it’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, is it fit to be regarded thus:
‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“No, sir.”
“Is feeling …
perception …
choices …
consciousness permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.” …
“So you should truly see …
Seeing this …
They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ vakkaliṁ iminā ovādena ovaditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā yena gijjhakūṭo pabbato tena pakkāmi.
verses.english: And then, after giving Venerable Vakkali this advice, the Buddha got up from his seat and went to the Vulture’s Peak Mountain.

verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā vakkali acirapakkantassa bhagavato upaṭṭhāke āmantesi:
verses.english: Then Venerable Vakkali addressed his carers,

verses.pali: “etha maṁ, āvuso, mañcakaṁ āropetvā yena isigilipassaṁ kāḷasilā tenupasaṅkamatha.
verses.english: “Come on, reverends, lift my cot and take me to the Black Rock on the slopes of Isigili.

verses.pali: Kathañhi nāma mādiso antaraghare kālaṁ kattabbaṁ maññeyyā”ti?
verses.english: For how on earth could one such as I imagine dying in an inhabited area!”

verses.pali: “Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato vakkalissa paṭissutvā āyasmantaṁ vakkaliṁ mañcakaṁ āropetvā yena isigilipassaṁ kāḷasilā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu.
verses.english: “Yes, reverend,” replied those mendicants, and did as he asked.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā tañca rattiṁ tañca divāvasesaṁ gijjhakūṭe pabbate vihāsi.
verses.english: Meanwhile, the Buddha spent the rest of that night and day on Vulture’s Peak Mountain.

verses.pali: Atha kho dve devatāyo abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ gijjhakūṭaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu …pe… ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu.
verses.english: Then, late at night, two glorious deities, lighting up the entire Vulture’s Peak, went up to the Buddha, bowed, and stood to one side.

verses.pali: Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho ekā devatā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: One deity said to him,
“Sir, the mendicant Vakkali is intent on liberation!”
And another deity said to him,
“He’ll definitely be well freed!”
This is what those deities said.

verses.pali: Idaṁ vatvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyiṁsu.
verses.english: Then they bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on their right side, before vanishing right there.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā tassā rattiyā accayena bhikkhū āmantesi:
verses.english: Then, when the night had passed, the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

verses.pali: “etha tumhe, bhikkhave, yena vakkali bhikkhu tenupasaṅkamatha; upasaṅkamitvā vakkaliṁ bhikkhuṁ evaṁ vadetha:
verses.english: “Come, mendicants, go to the mendicant Vakkali and tell him:

verses.pali: ‘Suṇāvuso tvaṁ, vakkali, bhagavato vacanaṁ dvinnañca devatānaṁ.
verses.english: ‘Vakkali, hear the word of the Buddha and two deities.

verses.pali: Imaṁ, āvuso, rattiṁ dve devatāyo abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ gijjhakūṭaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu.
verses.english: Late last night, two glorious deities, lighting up the entire Vulture’s Peak, went up to the Buddha, bowed, and stood to one side.

verses.pali: Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho, āvuso, ekā devatā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca—
verses.english: One deity said to him,
“Sir, the mendicant Vakkali is intent on liberation!”
The other deity said to him,

verses.pali: so hi nūna, bhante, suvimutto vimuccissatīti.
verses.english: “He’ll definitely be well freed!”

verses.pali: Bhagavā ca taṁ, āvuso vakkali, evamāha—
verses.english: And the Buddha said,
“Do not fear, Vakkali,
do not fear!

verses.pali: Apāpakaṁ te maraṇaṁ bhavissati, apāpikā kālakiriyā’”ti.
verses.english: Your death will not be a bad one; your passing will not be a bad one.”’”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paṭissutvā yenāyasmā vakkali tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ vakkaliṁ etadavocuṁ:
verses.english: “Yes, sir,” those monks replied. They went to Vakkali and said to him:
“Vakkali, hear the word of the Buddha and two deities.”

verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā vakkali upaṭṭhāke āmantesi:
verses.english: Then Vakkali addressed his carers,
“Please, reverends, help me off my cot.

verses.pali: Kathañhi nāma mādiso ucce āsane nisīditvā tassa bhagavato sāsanaṁ sotabbaṁ maññeyyā”ti.
verses.english: For how on earth could one such as I presume to listen to the Buddha’s instructions sitting on a high seat?”

verses.pali: “Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato vakkalissa paṭissutvā āyasmantaṁ vakkaliṁ mañcakā oropesuṁ.
verses.english: “Yes, reverend,” replied those mendicants, and helped him off his cot.

verses.pali: “Imaṁ, āvuso, rattiṁ dve devatāyo abhikkantāya rattiyā …pe… ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu.
verses.english: They repeated what the Buddha had said.

verses.pali: Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho, āvuso, ekā devatā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
Bhagavā ca taṁ, āvuso vakkali, evamāha:
Apāpakaṁ te maraṇaṁ bhavissati, apāpikā kālakiriyā’”ti.
“Tena hāvuso, mama vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatha:
verses.english: Vakkali said, “Well then, reverends, in my name bow with your head at the Buddha’s feet. Say to him:
‘Sir, the mendicant Vakkali is sick, suffering, gravely ill.
He bows with his head to your feet.’
And then say:
‘Form is impermanent.
I have no doubt of that.
I’m certain that what is impermanent is suffering.

verses.pali: Yadaniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, natthi me tattha chando vā rāgo vā pemaṁ vāti na vicikicchāmi.
verses.english: And I’m certain that I have no desire or greed or fondness for what is impermanent, suffering, and perishable.
Feeling is impermanent …

verses.pali: Yadaniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, natthi me tattha chando vā rāgo vā pemaṁ vāti na vicikicchāmi.

verses.english: Perception is impermanent …
Choices are impermanent …

verses.pali: Yadaniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, natthi me tattha chando vā rāgo vā pemaṁ vāti na vicikicchāmi.

verses.english: Consciousness is impermanent.
I have no doubt of that.
I’m certain that what is impermanent is suffering.

verses.pali: Yadaniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, natthi me tattha chando vā rāgo vā pemaṁ vāti na vicikicchāmī’”ti.
verses.english: And I’m certain that I have no desire or greed or fondness for what is impermanent, suffering, and perishable.’”

verses.pali: “Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato vakkalissa paṭissutvā pakkamiṁsu.
verses.english: “Yes, reverend,” those monks replied, and left.

verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā vakkali acirapakkantesu tesu bhikkhūsu satthaṁ āharesi.
verses.english: And then, not long after those mendicants had left, Venerable Vakkali committed suicide.

verses.pali: Atha kho te bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
verses.english: Then those mendicants went up to the Buddha and told him Vakkali’s message.

verses.pali: Yadaniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, natthi me tattha chando vā rāgo vā pemaṁ vāti na vicikicchāmi.
Yadaniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, natthi me tattha chando vā rāgo vā pemaṁ vāti na vicikicchāmī’”ti.

verses.english: Then the Buddha said to the mendicants,
“Come, mendicants, let’s go to the Black Rock on the slopes of Isigili,
where Vakkali, the gentleman, committed suicide.”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
verses.english: “Yes, sir,” they replied.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṁ yena isigilipassaṁ kāḷasilā tenupasaṅkami.
verses.english: Then the Buddha together with several mendicants went to the Black Rock on the slopes of Isigili.

verses.pali: Addasā kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ vakkaliṁ dūratova mañcake vivattakkhandhaṁ semānaṁ.
verses.english: The Buddha saw Vakkali off in the distance on his cot, lying with aggregates cast off.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena dhūmāyitattaṁ timirāyitattaṁ gacchateva purimaṁ disaṁ, gacchati pacchimaṁ disaṁ, gacchati uttaraṁ disaṁ, gacchati dakkhiṇaṁ disaṁ, gacchati uddhaṁ disaṁ, gacchati adho disaṁ, gacchati anudisaṁ.
verses.english: Now at that time a cloud of black smoke was moving east, west, north, south, above, below, and in-between.
The Buddha said to the mendicants,

verses.pali: “passatha no tumhe, bhikkhave, etaṁ dhūmāyitattaṁ timirāyitattaṁ gacchateva purimaṁ disaṁ …pe… gacchati anudisan”ti.
verses.english: “Mendicants, do you see that cloud of black smoke moving east, west, north, south, above, below, and in-between?”
“Yes, sir.”

verses.pali: “Eso kho, bhikkhave, māro pāpimā vakkalissa kulaputtassa viññāṇaṁ samanvesati:
verses.english: “That’s Māra the Wicked searching for Vakkali’s consciousness, wondering:
‘Where is Vakkali’s consciousness established?’

verses.pali: Appatiṭṭhitena ca, bhikkhave, viññāṇena vakkali kulaputto parinibbuto”ti.
verses.english: But since his consciousness is not established, Vakkali is quenched.”
